First Harvest Estimate Points To Larger Wheat And Oat Supplies

OSTARA, Kestria, Aug. 19, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative estimates that its members will harvest 184,000 tonnes of wheat and 52,000 tonnes of oats this season. The figures cover 426 farms across Kestria and are based on field inspections, planted area records and reports submitted by members up to 18 August.

The wheat estimate is 8 per cent above last season's final total, while oats are estimated to rise by 5 per cent. Fields around Amberford have the strongest yield prospects. Crops near Ostara show more variation following a dry spell during grain development.

These are field estimates, rather than grain already available for sale. Rain, harvesting conditions and the amount retained on farms may affect deliveries. Buyers seeking wheat or oats can obtain indicative supply information from the co-operative's sales desks in Amberford, Kestrel Bay and Saltmarsh.

Amberford Receiving Yard Introduces Separate Queues For Wheat And Oats

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Aug. 21, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has introduced separate wheat and oat queues at its Amberford receiving yard. The change follows a trial involving 38 deliveries, during which the average time from arrival to unloading fell from 54 minutes to 37 minutes. Both lanes use the existing weighbridge.

Drivers must identify their crop and booking reference at the entrance before joining a queue. Loads still require sampling, weighing and acceptance checks. A separate holding area is available for vehicles whose grain needs further testing, allowing other accepted loads to move through the yard.

The yard has received 2,640 tonnes of new-season grain so far, mostly wheat from farms south of Amberford. Members without a booking should contact the receiving office before travelling. The co-operative has also added clear signs at the approach road and pedestrian crossing beside the sampling room.

Early Wheat Samples Show Firm Protein And Low Moisture

OSTARA, Kestria, Sept. 7, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- The first new-season quality report from Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative shows average wheat protein of 12.6 per cent and average moisture of 13.2 per cent. The report covers 186 accepted loads, representing 5,920 tonnes delivered to the Amberford and Ostara receiving sites by 6 September.

Average wheat test weight was 78.4 kilogrammes per hectolitre. These results support the sale of several parcels for milling, although each customer contract has its own requirements. The samples mainly represent earlier-harvested fields and should not be treated as a measure of the whole crop.

Oat deliveries remain limited, with 740 tonnes accepted so far. Members can request the test results for their own loads through the receiving office. Any request for a second test must identify the delivery ticket, allowing staff to locate the sealed sample retained from that load.

September Purchase Notice Sets Wheat And Oat Base Prices

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Sept. 14, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has set its posted purchase price at KRN 286 per tonne for standard milling wheat and KRN 218 per tonne for standard food oats. The prices apply to new purchase agreements accepted from 14 September for grain delivered to the Amberford receiving site.

The wheat price assumes moisture no higher than 14 per cent and protein of at least 12 per cent. The oat price assumes moisture no higher than 13.5 per cent and test weight of at least 52 kilogrammes per hectolitre. Other quality requirements remain available from the buying desk.

These are prices paid to supplying members, rather than delivered selling prices for customers. Haulage, drying and any agreed quality adjustments are shown separately on settlement statements. Existing fixed-price agreements retain their agreed terms. Members should obtain a purchase reference before sending grain against the new notice.

Rain Raises Drying Demand At Ostara Grain Receiving Site

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 16, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Rain around Ostara has increased the proportion of wheat deliveries requiring drying at Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's local receiving site. Of the 61 wheat loads sampled during the past two days, 24 exceeded the standard moisture limit of 14 per cent. Accepted wet grain is being stored separately.

The site's dryer has processed 460 tonnes since the rain began. Members are being given a moisture reading and an estimated drying charge before unloading. The charge depends on the moisture removed and is separate from the purchase price shown on the member's grain agreement.

Receiving staff have reduced the number of wet-grain bookings to match drying capacity. Dry wheat and oat bookings remain available, subject to storage space. Members should report their latest moisture reading when arranging a delivery and should not mix damp grain with a dry load to meet the acceptance limit.

Harvest Review Trims Wheat Estimate As Oat Outlook Holds

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 28, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has revised its member wheat harvest estimate to 179,500 tonnes, down from the August estimate of 184,000 tonnes. The oat estimate is now 52,400 tonnes, compared with 52,000 tonnes previously. The review uses completed field records and updated reports received by 27 September.

Lower wheat yields around Ostara account for most of the reduction. Amberford results remain close to the earlier estimate. Members report that 81 per cent of their wheat area and 69 per cent of their oat area has been harvested, leaving uncertainty around the remaining fields.

The co-operative has accepted 96,800 tonnes of wheat and 21,600 tonnes of oats into its stores. These intake figures exclude grain still held on farms and must not be added to the harvest estimate. Customer allocations remain covered by accepted stocks and grain secured under existing member delivery agreements.
